results.title: Ghana’s black gold and the quest for value
results.content: The modern era of Ghana's petroleum industry began with the establishment of the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) in 1983 under the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation Act (PNDCL 64). The GNPC was mandated to lead the nation's efforts to explore oil and gas resources efficiently. For decades, the sector saw exploratory efforts that eventually culminated in major commercial discoveries, transforming Ghana into a notable player in the West African energy market and requiring a robust, multi-tiered regulatory framework to manage the newfound wealth. The Jubilee Milestone While exploration began in the late 19th century, the watershed moment arrived in 2007 with the discovery of the Jubilee Field deep waters off the coast of the Western Region. results.title: Ghanaian startup launches SMS-based AI platform to reach young people without internet access
results.content: A Ghanaian technology startup, Scopeg AI, is partnering with the Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment to expand access to artificial intelligence through an SMS-based platform designed for people without internet access or smartphones. The platform, Funza AI, allows users to interact with artificial intelligence by sending text messages to a short code and receiving AI-generated responses within seconds. It is designed to work on basic mobile phones, including feature phones, across mobile networks without requiring an internet connection or data bundle. The initiative is intended to make AI-powered services more accessible to young people, students, farmers, small business owners and jobseekers who may otherwise be excluded by the cost of internet access and digital devices.

results.title: ‘New economy is old failed promises with new branding’ – Oppong Nkrumah
results.content: MP for Ofoase-Ayirebi, Chairman of the NPP Policy Committee and Ranking Member of Parliament’s Economy and Development Committee, Kojo Oppong Nkrumah has described the government’s proposed new economy agenda as a “scam”, accusing the administration of repackaging what he calls failed promises under a new name. Speaking at a press conference organised by the Minority in Parliament on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, the Ofoase-Ayirebi MP said the 2027 Budget would be marked by what he described as the rebranding of existing policies and the presentation of economic figures that do not reflect conditions faced by ordinary Ghanaians. “Now, what you will realise on Thursday is that the 2027 Budget will be characterised by two things: the new economy scam. And this new economy is a scam. It's the old failed promises which have been repackaged with a new branding, some new colours,” he said.
